taxonomyNote: Animal Diversity Web lists the family as Crocodylidae; NatureServe gives Alligatoridae, used here.
fieldMarks: Blackish or olive-drab above; young have bold yellowish crossbands that may persist faintly in adults
Broadly rounded snout; no conspicuous upward-protruding lower teeth when the mouth is closed
Adults generally 4 m or less (maximum about 5.8 m); males much larger than females
behavior: Spring courtship includes loud bellowing and head slaps on the water
Inactive or less active from about late November to March in the northern range
Digs dens in banks and 'gator holes' used in cold spells and drought
Opportunistic feeder: invertebrates and small fish when young; birds, reptiles and mammals as large adults
habitat: Fresh and brackish marshes, ponds, lakes, rivers, swamps, bayous and canals; basks on logs or banks.
range: Coastal North Carolina to the Florida Keys, west to southern Texas, north to southeastern Oklahoma and Arkansas. Not native to Canada.

lookalikes.name: American crocodile
lookalikes.howToTell: Narrower snout and a fourth lower tooth that protrudes upward near the snout tip.

lookalikes.name: Spectacled caiman
lookalikes.howToTell: Has a curved bony crosswise ridge in front of the eyes, which the alligator lacks.
